title: bot.ability.listening.speech.output
description: One Listening speech observation after voice detection: content plus relative voice spans. content_type is audio/pcm while the observation is acoustic and text/plain once speech decoding has rewritten it into words. Empty segments means no voice in this observation (including silence used to close a turn).

event.description: Canonical HSM event name that emitted this upstream payload.
event.title: Event

data.description: Complete typed payload emitted by the upstream event.

audio.description: Reference (a URI reference) to the audio this stimulus carries; floppy passes media by reference, never as bytes [floppy field].
audio.title: Audio

media_type.description: Optional media type or codec label, such as audio/pcm or audio/opus.
media_type.title: Media Type

sample_rate_hz.description: Optional sample rate for raw or decoded audio, measured in hertz.
sample_rate_hz.title: Sample Rate Hz

channels.description: Optional number of audio channels represented by the chunk.
channels.title: Channels

kind.description: Optional low-cardinality acoustic provenance hint. Prefer domain-qualified labels when the source is clear (for example phone.ringing, phone.call, ambient, knock) so models do not confuse bare tokens like ring. Not a linguistic interpretation.
kind.title: Kind

amplitude_db.description: Optional loudness of this sound at its source, in dB SPL measured one metre away. A shout and a whisper leave the same mouth, so loudness belongs to the sound rather than to the thing that made it. How far it carries is the environment's to work out; omitting this means the sound reaches every listener regardless of distance.
amplitude_db.title: Amplitude Db

received_level_db.description: Optional loudness of this sound in dB SPL where the recipient of this event is, which is a different quantity from amplitude_db: the same shout is one level at the mouth and another at the far side of the room. The environment fills this in per recipient, so an emitter never sets it. None means the environment had nothing to measure — the sound carried no amplitude, or nobody said where it or the listener was — not that the sound was silent.
received_level_db.title: Received Level Db

source.description: Optional acoustic source: the transducer this sound came off, as its emitter stamps it (speaking stamps its mouth, "speaking", the mouth its efference copy names). An SCXML event relayed through the body keeps only its data, so the source travels in the sound itself [floppy field]. Listening scores an arrival against an efference copy only when this is the producing mouth; a sound without one is never the bot's own.
source.title: Source

participants.description: Who produced this stimulus, stamped by the device that emitted it. Empty when the device knows no one (ambient sound, an unattended camera).

items.description: Someone who took part in a stimulus: an opaque, producer-stable identity reference and the role it played (source: who produced it; target: who it was addressed to).

ref.description: Opaque, producer-stable identity such as a phone number, an app person id, or a chat handle. Never a display name chosen by the bot.
ref.title: Ref

role.description: source: who produced the stimulus (speaker, sender). target: who it was addressed to.
role.title: Role

own.description: True when the producer knows this participant is the bot itself, for example the bot's own voice heard back or the voice it spoke with. Stamped only by that producer; never inferred.
own.title: Own

resembles.description: For an identity its producer made just now (nobody it knew): the known identities it resembles, best first, at most 3. Stamped only by that producer; never a link.

items.description: A known identity this new one resembles: its ref and how similar the two are (-1..1). Perception data only: it links nothing, and it is never a print.

ref.description: The ref of the known identity, as its producer stamps it.
ref.title: Ref

similarity.description: How similar the two are, -1..1; higher is more alike.
similarity.title: Similarity

resembles.title: Resembles

items.title: Participant

participants.title: Participants

data.title: SoundData

id.description: Upstream HSM event correlation id, when the emitter stamped one.
id.title: Id

source.description: Upstream HSM event source identity, when stamped by its producer.
source.title: Source

target.description: Upstream HSM event target identity, when stamped for delivery.
target.title: Target

parent.description: The exact environment.sound event and typed payload that produced this speech observation. This causal parent is carried in domain data, not event metadata.

content.description: The one payload this observation carries: the audio while content_type is audio/pcm, the decoded words once content_type is text/plain. PCM observations on the same conversation stream are homogeneous so turn assembly can concatenate their bytes. While content_type is audio/pcm, content is a reference (a URI reference) to the audio; floppy passes media by reference, never as bytes [floppy field].
content.title: Content

content_type.description: Media type of content. audio/pcm before speech decoding, text/plain after it rewrites this observation into words.
content_type.title: Content Type

start_seconds.description: Optional start time of this clipped voice segment in the source audio.
start_seconds.title: Start Seconds

end_seconds.description: Optional exclusive end time of this clipped voice segment in the source audio.
end_seconds.title: End Seconds

confidence.description: Optional diarizer confidence for this clipped speech segment.
confidence.title: Confidence

source_ids.description: Opaque source identities for this speech observation. Empty source_ids are permitted when Listening has speech evidence but no identity classifier result; Conversation rejects them.
source_ids.title: Source Ids

voice_detection.description: Voice spans from VoiceDetection relative to the start of this observation.

segments.description: Voice spans in the inspected audio, ordered by ascending start_seconds. Empty means no voice.

items.description: One voice span in the inspected audio, measured from the start of that input.

start_seconds.description: Inclusive start of this voice span, in seconds from the beginning of the inspected audio input.
start_seconds.title: Start Seconds

end_seconds.description: Exclusive end of this voice span, in seconds from the beginning of the inspected audio input.
end_seconds.title: End Seconds

confidence.description: Optional provider confidence for this span, normalized from 0.0 to 1.0 when available.
confidence.title: Confidence

items.title: VoiceDetectionSegment

segments.title: Segments

voice_detection.title: ApplyData

anyOf.description: The tone heard in a voice: an affect label, the classifier's score per affect class, valence from negative to positive, and the classifier's confidence in the label.

label.description: The affect class the voice sounded most like, as the classifier names it.
label.title: Label

scores.description: The classifier's score from 0 to 1 for each affect class it knows; empty when it gives none.
scores.title: Scores

valence.description: How positive the voice sounded, from -1 (negative) to 1 (positive), when the classifier says.
valence.title: Valence

confidence.description: The classifier's confidence in the label, from 0 to 1, when it says.
confidence.title: Confidence

affect.description: The tone this speech was said in, heard in its longest voice: an affect label with the classifier's scores, valence and confidence. Present only on decoded (text) speech when an affect classifier is composed and answered in time; a perception, not a judgment.
affect.title: Affect

sample_rate_hz.description: Sample rate of audio in hertz (required to place the observation on a conversation timeline).
sample_rate_hz.title: Sample Rate Hz

media_type.description: Validated media type for the signed 16-bit PCM audio bytes.
media_type.title: Media Type

participants.description: Who produced the sound this speech was decoded from, copied from the admitted environment.sound chunks. Listening never works out who someone is; it only carries what the device stamped.

items.description: Someone who took part in a stimulus: an opaque, producer-stable identity reference and the role it played (source: who produced it; target: who it was addressed to).

ref.description: Opaque, producer-stable identity such as a phone number, an app person id, or a chat handle. Never a display name chosen by the bot.
ref.title: Ref

role.title: Role

ref.title: Ref
